# ImagePipeline

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Process-wide tuning for the image pipeline: decoding, resolution capping and compression.

Decoding a PNG, reducing it to its printed resolution and compressing the result are the most expensive things BonniePDF does to an image, and they depend only on the image. The pipeline therefore keeps the results of that work in a bounded in-memory cache, so a logo, letterhead or signature that appears on every generated document is processed once rather than once per document. The cache never changes the output; it only skips work already done.

Namespace `BonniePDF`.

## Properties

- [`CacheBytes`](#cachebytes): The memory, in bytes, the image cache currently holds against `CacheMaxBytes`.
- [`CacheMaxBytes`](#cachemaxbytes): The most memory, in bytes, the image cache may hold.
- [`CompressionLevel`](#compressionlevel): The compression applied to image pixel data (and image colour profiles) in every document written from now on.
- [`DefaultCacheMaxBytes`](#defaultcachemaxbytes): The default size of the image cache: 32 MiB.

### `CacheBytes`

```csharp
static long CacheBytes { get; }
```

### `CacheMaxBytes`

```csharp
static long CacheMaxBytes { get; set; }
```

*static*

The most memory, in bytes, the image cache may hold. It counts the decoded pixels and the original file bytes of each cached image (the compressed streams kept alongside are smaller and not counted). The least recently used images are dropped to stay within it, and an image larger than the whole budget is not cached. Set it to `0` to turn caching off, which also stops compressed streams being kept: nothing is retained between documents, at the cost of redoing the work for each one. Defaults to `DefaultCacheMaxBytes`.

### `CompressionLevel`

```csharp
static ImageCompressionLevel CompressionLevel { get; set; }
```

*static*

The compression applied to image pixel data (and image colour profiles) in every document written from now on. Defaults to `Balanced`.

